claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 can be homogenized at high temperature into a single-phase BCC structure.
The high-temperature BCC state of Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is disordered.
High mixing entropy stabilizes the disordered BCC state at high temperature.
Cooling to an intermediate temperature reduces the configurational-entropy contribution to stability.
The alloy has a thermodynamic driving force for formation of B2 or a related ordered phase.
The Al concentration in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 contributes to the thermodynamic driving force for local ordering.
Kinetic hindrance normally retards the ordering transformation.
At approximately 600°C, diffusion is sufficiently active to permit ordering in this alloy.
Isothermal annealing permits nucleation and growth of ordered regions within the metastable BCC matrix.
Formation and growth of ordered regions destabilize the initial disordered BCC state.
Samples annealed at approximately 600°C will develop superlattice reflections indicative of ordering.
Annealed samples will exhibit microscopy evidence of an ordered B2 or similar phase.
The fraction of the ordered phase will increase with annealing time at approximately 600°C.
Rapidly quenched samples will retain the single-phase disordered BCC structure.
At extremely low temperatures, frozen diffusion prevents the proposed ordering mechanism from operating.
At temperatures well above the ordering onset, the proposed ordering mechanism does not apply.
Failure of annealed samples to develop an ordered phase or a time-dependent increase in ordered-phase fraction relative to quenched controls would falsify the proposed mechanism.
